title: Habituation (pharmacoresistance) occurs in every testable pathway model

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Habituation (pharmacoresistance) occurs in every testable pathway model

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Modelling pharmacoresistance as habituation (a progressive 50% drop in response across repeated, lengthening stimulations), at least one habituating stimulus–response pair was found in each of the 27 testable BioModels pathway models, with 1–50% of node pairs per model habituating.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 2. Results › 2.7. Making and Breaking Pharmacoresistance

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Overall, we were able to test 27 out of the 35 models (77%, see Section 4) and at least one instance of habituation was found for each model, with the distribution of pharmacoresistance across all potential models ranging between 1–50% (see Figure 8 and Figures S11–S13).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Biswas S, Clawson W, Levin M, “Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions”, International journal of molecular sciences (2022), doi:10.3390/ijms24010285; section “2. Results › 2.7. Making and Breaking Pharmacoresistance”. Scope: 27 ODE pathway models from BioModels

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-grn-learning-14: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.91

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The exact model-level claim has explicit thresholds and public inputs. It is directly reproducible, though its pharmacological interpretation is not established by the simulation alone.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Apply the six-stimulation protocol and 50% progressive-response criterion to every eligible node pair in the 27 testable models. Reproduce whether every model has at least one qualifying pair and the per-model 1-50% range.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Eight models were not testable under the protocol.

The simulated habituation criterion is only a proxy for pharmacoresistance.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.9
analysis feasibility: 0.84
data adequacy: 0.88
operationalizability: 0.97
discriminating power: 0.92

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The 50 percent criterion, the six increasing epochs and the 27-model denominator are explicit, and the repository contains the resistance screen plus result matrices. Re-running or reanalysing that screen can confirm or refute both the universal occurrence and the 1–50 percent band. The pharmacoresistance label is the authors' mapping, but the numerical claim is about the ODE assay.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Apply six lengthening UCS stimulations and score a node pair as habituating when the response falls by at least half at each step. At least one such pair in each of the 27 testable models, with pair fractions between 1 and 50 percent, would confirm the claim; any testable model with zero pairs, or fractions outside that range, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Eight of the 35 models were dropped as untestable, so the 'every model' result is conditional on that filter.

Habituation here is a 50 percent ODE ratio, not a measured drug response.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.85
discriminating power: 0.74
analysis feasibility: 0.6
operationalizability: 0.92
data adequacy: 0.82
